beats.narration_text: Template "Yo Claude, [EMAIL] — make this more polite." User's email happens to open "Yo Claude." After substitution Claude reads the whole thing as the email and begins its rewrite "Dear Claude." Wrap the email in `<email>...</email>` and the confusion disappears.

beats.narration_text: A prompt template is crystal-clear to a human, but once user input is substituted in, Claude can't tell your instruction from the data it's supposed to act on.
Claude was trained to treat XML tags as an organizing mechanism; wrapping variable input in tags marks its start and end explicitly, so the model stops guessing where the data ends.
beats.visual: A prompt template with a highlighted variable slot; on substitution the highlight dissolves into surrounding text, then XML tags snap back around it

beats.narration_text: `<email>Yo Claude, thx 4 the help</email>` → polished rewrite; without tags → "Dear Claude…".
Claude was trained to treat XML tags as an organizing mechanism; wrapping variable input in tags marks its start and end explicitly, so the model stops guessing where the data ends.

Your turn. Paste this: your Claude prompt template substitutes a user's email into a polishing request, and when the email starts with 'Yo Claude,' Claude reads the whole thing as the email and writes back 'Dear Claude.' Ask Claude to show you why this happens, how wrapping the substituted content in delimiter tags fixes it, and what the general rule is for when variable substitution needs delimiter tags.

props.command: My Claude prompt template substitutes a user's email into a polishing request, and when the email starts with 'Yo Claude,' Claude reads the whole thing as the email and begins its rewrite 'Dear Claude.' Show me why this happens, how wrapping the substituted content in `<email>...</email>` tags fixes it, and what the general rule is for when variable substitution needs delimiter tags.
